1: #!/usr/bin/env node
2: "use strict";
3: 
4: /**
5:  * MCP acceptance harness — Phase 0.2 discovery baseline.
6:  *
7:  * A standalone black-box harness that targets a configurable production-component
8:  * MCP endpoint and asserts the public OAuth discovery contract:
9:  *
10:  *   A1  an unauthenticated JSON-RPC `initialize` request receives HTTP 401
11:  *       (an OAuth challenge), not a protocol-dispatch error (e.g. HTTP 400
12:  *       with JSON-RPC -32601 "Method not found");
13:  *   A2  the 401 challenge carries a Bearer `WWW-Authenticate` header whose
14:  *       `resource_metadata` parameter is the configured public
15:  *       protected-resource metadata URL (the MCP endpoint origin plus
16:  *       `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`) and never a loopback or lab
17:  *       URL (e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:3001/...`);
18:  *   A3  the protected-resource metadata document parses as JSON and names the
19:  *       configured authorization-server issuer in `authorization_servers`;
20:  *   A4  the authorization-server metadata document parses as JSON and supplies
21:  *       usable `authorization_endpoint`, `token_endpoint`,
22:  *       `registration_endpoint`, and `jwks_uri` values (absolute http(s)
23:  *       URLs; https when the issuer is public).
24:  *
25:  * Baseline expectation (Phase 0.2): against the current production component,
26:  * A1, A2, and A4 FAIL and A3 passes. Verified current state (2026-09-17,
27:  * docs/MCP-PRODUCTION-FIX-PLAN.md):
28:  *   - `initialize` returns HTTP 400 with JSON-RPC -32601 (mcp-server/src/gateway.rs
29:  *     only recognizes tools/list and tools/call), so no 401 challenge is ever
30:  *     issued for the initial request;
31:  *   - the 401 builders that do exist hard-code the lab loopback URL
32:  *     `http://127.0.0.1:3001` (mcp-server/src/gateway.rs:456-541);
33:  *   - `https://mcal.hajnal.space/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` is valid
34:  *     JSON advertising `https://cal.hajnal.space` (A3 passes);
35:  *   - `https://cal.hajnal.space/.well-known/openid-configuration` returns the
36:  *     CommonCal SPA HTML, not authorization-server metadata (A4 fails).
37:  *
38:  * The harness asserts the target contract and therefore exits non-zero against
39:  * the current production component. That failure is the intentional, asserted
40:  * exit condition for this phase: it documents the current broken state that
41:  * later phases must fix. The harness is a regression gate: it stays red until
42:  * the production component implements the public challenge and discovery.
43:  *
44:  * This harness does NOT launch or depend on the slice1-lab binaries, and it
45:  * does not treat the lab binary as a release artifact. It reuses the Phase 0.1
46:  * `initialize` request fixture (mcp-acceptance/fixtures/initialize-request.json)
47:  * and the MCP/OAuth standards-compliance expectations. It is a pure HTTP
48:  * client: it starts no servers and leaves no processes behind.
49:  *
50:  * Configuration (command-line flags, then environment variables, then defaults):
51:  *   --url / MCP_URL             MCP endpoint URL (default: https://mcal.hajnal.space/mcp)
52:  *   --issuer / MCP_OAUTH_ISSUER configured authorization-server issuer
53:  *                               (default: https://cal.hajnal.space)
54:  *   --timeout-ms / MCP_TIMEOUT_MS              request timeout ms (default: 15000)
55:  *   --record-dir / MCP_RECORD_DIR              record directory (default: OS temp dir)
56:  *
57:  * Exit codes:
58:  *   0  all discovery assertions pass (PASS)
59:  *   1  one or more discovery assertions fail (FAIL) — the intentional Phase 0.2
60:  *      baseline exit condition against the current production component
61:  *   2  harness error (invalid configuration, network failure, unexpected error)
62:  */
63: 
64: const fs = require("node:fs");
65: const os = require("node:os");
66: const path = require("node:path");
67: 
68: const HARNESS_NAME = "commoncal-mcp-acceptance";
69: const HARNESS_VERSION = "0.2.0";
70: 
71: const DEFAULTS = {
72:   url: "https://mcal.hajnal.space/mcp",
73:   issuer: "https://cal.hajnal.space",
74:   timeoutMs: 15000,
75: };
76: 
77: class HarnessError extends Error {}
78: 
79: function env(name, fallback) {
80:   const v = process.env[name];
81:   return v === undefined || v === "" ? fallback : v;
82: }
83: 
84: /**
85:  * Parse command-line flags. Returns a map of flag -> value. Unknown flags are
86:  * collected under the `_unknown` key so they can be reported as a config error.
87:  */
88: function parseArgs(argv) {
89:   const flags = {};
90:   const unknown = [];
91:   for (let i = 0; i < argv.length; i++) {
92:     const arg = argv[i];
93:     if (arg === "--help" || arg === "-h") {
94:       flags.help = true;
95:       continue;
96:     }
97:     if (arg.startsWith("--")) {
98:       const eq = arg.indexOf("=");
99:       let name;
100:       let value;
101:       if (eq !== -1) {
102:         name = arg.slice(2, eq);
103:         value = arg.slice(eq + 1);
104:       } else {
105:         name = arg.slice(2);
106:         const next = argv[i + 1];
107:         if (next !== undefined && !next.startsWith("--")) {
108:           value = next;
109:           i++;
110:         } else {
111:           value = "true";
112:         }
113:       }
114:       flags[name] = value;
115:     } else {
116:       unknown.push(arg);
117:     }
118:   }
119:   flags._unknown = unknown;
120:   return flags;
121: }
122: 
123: function printHelp() {
124:   console.log(`Usage: node mcp-acceptance/discovery.js [options]
125: 
126: Options:
127:   --url <url>              MCP endpoint URL (default: ${DEFAULTS.url})
128:   --issuer <url>           configured authorization-server issuer (default: ${DEFAULTS.issuer})
129:   --timeout-ms <n>         request timeout in ms (default: ${DEFAULTS.timeoutMs})
130:   --record-dir <dir>       directory for the deterministic record (default: OS temp dir)
131:   -h, --help               show this help
132: 
133: Environment variables MCP_URL, MCP_OAUTH_ISSUER, MCP_TIMEOUT_MS, and
134: MCP_RECORD_DIR are also honored; command-line flags take precedence.
135: `);
136: }
137: 
138: function describeError(err) {
139:   if (err === undefined || err === null) return "unknown error";
140:   if (typeof err === "string") return err;
141:   return err.message || String(err);
142: }
143: 
144: /**
145:  * Resolve a configuration value from (in order of precedence): command-line
146:  * flag, environment variable, default.
147:  */
148: function resolve(flags, flagName, envName, fallback) {
149:   if (flags[flagName] !== undefined) return flags[flagName];
150:   return env(envName, fallback);
151: }
152: 
153: function loadConfig(flags) {
154:   const url = resolve(flags, "url", "MCP_URL", DEFAULTS.url);
155:   let parsed;
156:   try {
157:     parsed = new URL(url);
158:   } catch {
159:     throw new HarnessError(`MCP_URL is not a valid URL: ${url}`);
160:   }
161:   if (parsed.protocol !== "http:" && parsed.protocol !== "https:") {
162:     throw new HarnessError(`MCP_URL must use http or https: ${url}`);
163:   }
164: 
165:   const issuer = resolve(flags, "issuer", "MCP_OAUTH_ISSUER", DEFAULTS.issuer);
166:   let issuerParsed;
167:   try {
168:     issuerParsed = new URL(issuer);
169:   } catch {
170:     throw new HarnessError(`MCP_OAUTH_ISSUER is not a valid URL: ${issuer}`);
171:   }
172:   if (issuerParsed.protocol !== "http:" && issuerParsed.protocol !== "https:") {
173:     throw new HarnessError(`MCP_OAUTH_ISSUER must use http or https: ${issuer}`);
174:   }
175: 
176:   const timeoutRaw = resolve(flags, "timeout-ms", "MCP_TIMEOUT_MS", String(DEFAULTS.timeoutMs));
177:   const timeoutMs = Number(timeoutRaw);
178:   if (!Number.isFinite(timeoutMs) || timeoutMs <= 0) {
179:     throw new HarnessError(`MCP_TIMEOUT_MS must be a positive number: ${timeoutRaw}`);
180:   }
181: 
182:   return {
183:     url,
184:     issuer,
185:     timeoutMs,
186:     recordDir: resolve(flags, "record-dir", "MCP_RECORD_DIR", os.tmpdir()),
187:   };
188: }
189: 
190: /**
191:  * The configured public protected-resource metadata URL: the MCP endpoint
192:  * origin plus the RFC 9728 well-known path. This mirrors the production
193:  * configuration logic (mcp-server/src/config.rs) and the fix-plan requirement
194:  * to derive resource_metadata from MCP_PUBLIC_RESOURCE_URL.
195:  */
196: function expectedResourceMetadataUrl(mcpUrl) {
197:   const u = new URL(mcpUrl);
198:   return `${u.origin}/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`;
199: }
200: 
201: /**
202:  * True for loopback hosts: the 127.0.0.0/8 range, ::1, localhost, and 0.0.0.0.
203:  * The current production 401 builders hard-code the lab loopback URL
204:  * http://127.0.0.1:3001 (mcp-server/src/gateway.rs:456-541); this is the
205:  * "loopback or lab URL" the A2 assertion must reject.
206:  */
207: function isLoopbackHost(host) {
208:   if (!host) return false;
209:   const h = host.toLowerCase();
210:   if (h === "localhost" || h === "::1" || h === "0.0.0.0") return true;
211:   if (h === "127.0.0.1" || h.startsWith("127.")) return true;
212:   return false;
213: }
214: 
215: function isLoopbackUrl(rawUrl) {
216:   try {
217:     return isLoopbackHost(new URL(rawUrl).hostname);
218:   } catch {
219:     return false;
220:   }
221: }
222: 
223: /**
224:  * Load the `initialize` request fixture shared with the Phase 0.1 harness.
225:  */
226: function loadInitializeFixture() {
227:   const fixturePath = path.join(__dirname, "fixtures", "initialize-request.json");
228:   let raw;
229:   try {
230:     raw = fs.readFileSync(fixturePath, "utf8");
231:   } catch (err) {
232:     throw new HarnessError(
233:       `cannot read initialize fixture ${fixturePath}: ${describeError(err)}`
234:     );
235:   }
236:   let fixture;
237:   try {
238:     fixture = JSON.parse(raw);
239:   } catch (err) {
240:     throw new HarnessError(
241:       `initialize fixture ${fixturePath} is not valid JSON: ${describeError(err)}`
242:     );
243:   }
244:   if (
245:     !isPlainObject(fixture) ||
246:     fixture.method !== "initialize" ||
247:     !isPlainObject(fixture.params)
248:   ) {
249:     throw new HarnessError(
250:       `initialize fixture ${fixturePath} must be a JSON-RPC initialize request with params`
251:     );
252:   }
253:   return fixture;
254: }
255: 
256: function buildInitializeRequest() {
257:   const fixture = loadInitializeFixture();
258:   return {
259:     ...fixture,
260:     id: 1,
261:     params: {
262:       ...fixture.params,
263:       clientInfo: { name: HARNESS_NAME, version: HARNESS_VERSION },
264:     },
265:   };
266: }
267: 
268: /**
269:  * Perform one HTTP request and capture the full response deterministically.
270:  */
271: async function httpProbe(cfg, method, url, body) {
272:   const headers = {};
273:   let bodyString = null;
274:   if (body !== null && body !== undefined) {
275:     bodyString = typeof body === "string" ? body : JSON.stringify(body);
276:     headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json";
277:   }
278:   if (method === "POST") {
279:     headers.Accept = "application/json, text/event-stream";
280:   }
281: 
282:   let status;
283:   let respHeaders;
284:   let rawBody;
285:   try {
286:     const controller = new AbortController();
287:     const timer = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), cfg.timeoutMs);
288:     let res;
289:     try {
290:       res = await fetch(url, {
291:         method,
292:         headers,
293:         body: bodyString,
294:         signal: controller.signal,
295:       });
296:     } finally {
297:       clearTimeout(timer);
298:     }
299:     status = res.status;
300:     respHeaders = normalizeHeaders(res.headers);
301:     rawBody = await res.text();
302:   } catch (err) {
303:     throw new HarnessError(`network failure contacting ${url}: ${describeError(err)}`);
304:   }
305: 
306:   let bodyJson = null;
307:   let bodyJsonParseError = null;
308:   try {
309:     bodyJson = JSON.parse(rawBody);
310:   } catch (err) {
311:     bodyJsonParseError = describeError(err);
312:   }
313: 
314:   return {
315:     status,
316:     headers: respHeaders,
317:     bodyRaw: rawBody,
318:     bodyJson,
319:     bodyJsonParseError,
320:   };
321: }
322: 
323: /**
324:  * Normalize response headers into a plain object, dropping volatile /
325:  * hop-by-hop headers so the recorded response is deterministic.
326:  */
327: function normalizeHeaders(headers) {
328:   const skip = new Set([
329:     "date",
330:     "x-request-id",
331:     "set-cookie",
332:     "transfer-encoding",
333:     "connection",
334:     "keep-alive",
335:   ]);
336:   const out = {};
337:   for (const [key, value] of headers.entries()) {
338:     const k = key.toLowerCase();
339:     if (skip.has(k)) continue;
340:     if (k in out) {
341:       out[k] = [].concat(out[k], value);
342:     } else {
343:       out[k] = value;
344:     }
345:   }
346:   return out;
347: }
348: 
349: function isPlainObject(v) {
350:   return v !== null && typeof v === "object" && !Array.isArray(v);
351: }
352: 
353: /**
354:  * Extract the resource_metadata parameter from a WWW-Authenticate header
355:  * value. Returns the raw parameter value or null when absent.
356:  */
357: function extractResourceMetadata(wwwAuthenticate) {
358:   if (typeof wwwAuthenticate !== "string") return null;
359:   const m = wwwAuthenticate.match(/resource_metadata\s*=\s*"([^"]*)"/i);
360:   if (m) return m[1];
361:   const bare = wwwAuthenticate.match(/resource_metadata\s*=\s*([^\s,]+)/i);
362:   if (bare) return bare[1];
363:   return null;
364: }
365: 
366: /**
367:  * A1: an unauthenticated JSON-RPC initialize request must receive HTTP 401
368:  * (an OAuth challenge), not a protocol-dispatch error.
369:  */
370: function assertA1(resp) {
371:   const violations = [];
372:   if (resp.status !== 401) {
373:     const detail = [];
374:     if (resp.bodyJsonParseError !== null) {
375:       detail.push(`body is not valid JSON (${resp.bodyJsonParseError})`);
376:     } else if (isPlainObject(resp.bodyJson) && resp.bodyJson.error) {
377:       const e = resp.bodyJson.error;
378:       detail.push(
379:         `JSON-RPC error ${e.code !== undefined ? e.code : "?"}: ${e.message || "(no message)"}`
380:       );
381:     }
382:     violations.push(
383:       `A1: unauthenticated initialize returned HTTP ${resp.status}${
384:         detail.length > 0 ? ` (${detail.join("; ")})` : ""
385:       }; expected HTTP 401 (OAuth challenge), not a protocol-dispatch error`
386:     );
387:   }
388:   return violations;
389: }
390: 
391: /**
392:  * A2: the 401 challenge must carry a Bearer WWW-Authenticate header whose
393:  * resource_metadata parameter is the configured public protected-resource
394:  * metadata URL, and never a loopback or lab URL.
395:  */
396: function assertA2(resp, expectedUrl, expectedIsLoopback) {
397:   const violations = [];
398:   const www = resp.headers["www-authenticate"];
399:   if (www === undefined) {
400:     violations.push(
401:       "A2: 401 response has no WWW-Authenticate header; expected a Bearer challenge with a resource_metadata parameter"
402:     );
403:     return violations;
404:   }
405:   if (!/^Bearer\s/i.test(www)) {
406:     violations.push(
407:       `A2: WWW-Authenticate is not a Bearer challenge: ${JSON.stringify(www)}`
408:     );
409:     return violations;
410:   }
411:   const resourceMetadata = extractResourceMetadata(www);
412:   if (resourceMetadata === null) {
413:     violations.push(
414:       `A2: Bearer challenge has no resource_metadata parameter: ${JSON.stringify(www)}`
415:     );
416:     return violations;
417:   }
418:   if (resourceMetadata !== expectedUrl) {
419:     violations.push(
420:       `A2: challenge resource_metadata is ${JSON.stringify(resourceMetadata)}; expected the configured public URL ${JSON.stringify(expectedUrl)}`
421:     );
422:   }
423:   if (!expectedIsLoopback) {
424:     if (isLoopbackUrl(resourceMetadata)) {
425:       violations.push(
426:         `A2: challenge resource_metadata points at a loopback/lab URL (${JSON.stringify(resourceMetadata)}); it must be the public URL`
427:       );
428:     }
429:     try {
430:       if (new URL(resourceMetadata).protocol !== "https:") {
431:         violations.push(
432:           `A2: challenge resource_metadata is not HTTPS: ${JSON.stringify(resourceMetadata)}`
433:         );
434:       }
435:     } catch {
436:       violations.push(

505:   if (!isPlainObject(doc.bodyJson)) {

514:     "token_endpoint",

9:  * deterministically. It is a self-contained, dependency-free OAuth provider
10:  * (DCR + Authorization Code + S256 PKCE + token exchange + JWKS) built on
11:  * Node built-ins only.
12:  *
13:  * It reuses the slice1-lab fixture shapes:
14:  *   - the DCR request shape (slice1-lab/negative_tests.py fresh_dcr,
15:  *     slice1-lab/auth-server/src/server.mjs validateRegisteredMetadata);
16:  *   - the standard access-token claim contract (slice1-lab/src/jwt.rs
17:  *     AccessClaims: iss, numeric sub, aud, exp, iat, client_id, scope, jti,

24:  * its own signing key (generated at startup), its own client/code/token
25:  * stores, and its own grant store.
26:  */

28: const crypto = require("node:crypto");
29: 
30: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
31: // Scope catalog (reused from slice1-lab/src/common.rs SCOPE_CATALOG)
32: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
33: 
34: const SCOPE_CATALOG = [
35:   "commoncal.calendar.metadata.read",
36:   "commoncal.availability.read",
37:   "commoncal.event.read.basic",
38:   "commoncal.event.read.details",
39:   "commoncal.event.create",
40:   "commoncal.event.update",
41:   "commoncal.event.delete",
42:   "commoncal.reminder.read",
43:   "commoncal.reminder.write",
44: ];
45: 
46: // A scope deliberately outside the catalog (slice1-lab/src/common.rs EVIL_SCOPE).
47: const EVIL_SCOPE = "evil.unknown.scope";
48: 
49: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
50: // base64url helpers
51: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
52: 
53: function b64urlEncode(buf) {
54:   return Buffer.from(buf).toString("base64url");
55: }
56: 
57: function b64urlDecode(str) {
58:   return Buffer.from(str, "base64url");
59: }
60: 
61: function b64urlJson(obj) {
62:   return b64urlEncode(JSON.stringify(obj));
63: }
64: 
65: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
66: // RSA key + JWK + RS256 JWT
67: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
68: 
69: /**
70:  * Generate an RSA key pair and expose the public key as a JWK (n, e) plus a
71:  * signing function. The private key never leaves this module.
72:  */
73: function createSigningKey(kid) {
74:   const { publicKey, privateKey } = crypto.generateKeyPairSync("rsa", {
75:     modulusLength: 2048,
76:     publicKeyEncoding: { type: "spki", format: "pem" },
77:     privateKeyEncoding: { type: "pkcs8", format: "pem" },
78:   });
79: 
80:   // Extract n and e from the SPKI public key.
81:   const keyObj = crypto.createPublicKey(publicKey);
82:   const jwk = keyObj.export({ format: "jwk" });
83: 
84:   return {
85:     kid,
86:     jwk: {
87:       kty: "RSA",
88:       n: jwk.n,
89:       e: jwk.e,
90:       use: "sig",
91:       alg: "RS256",
92:       kid,
93:     },
94:     sign(payload) {
95:       const signer = crypto.createSign("RSA-SHA256");
96:       signer.update(payload);
97:       signer.end();
98:       // Output encoding is base64url; the signature format is DER (PKCS#1 v1.5),
99:       // which is what RSA-SHA256 produces by default.
100:       return signer.sign(privateKey, "base64url");
101:     },
102:   };
103: }
104: 
105: /**
106:  * Sign a JWT (RS256) with the given claims and signing key.
107:  */
108: function signJwt(claims, signingKey) {
109:   const header = { alg: "RS256", typ: "JWT", kid: signingKey.kid };
110:   const signingInput = `${b64urlJson(header)}.${b64urlJson(claims)}`;
111:   const signature = signingKey.sign(signingInput);
112:   return `${signingInput}.${signature}`;
113: }
114: 
115: /**
116:  * Verify an RS256 JWT signature against a JWK. Returns true if valid.
117:  */
118: function verifyJwtSignature(jwt, jwk) {
119:   const parts = jwt.split(".");
120:   if (parts.length !== 3) return false;
121:   const [headerB64, payloadB64, signatureB64] = parts;
122:   let header;
123:   try {
124:     header = JSON.parse(b64urlDecode(headerB64).toString("utf8"));
125:   } catch {
126:     return false;
127:   }
128:   if (header.alg !== "RS256") return false;
129:   if (jwk.kty !== "RSA" || !jwk.n || !jwk.e) return false;
130: 
131:   // Reconstruct the RSA public key from the JWK (n, e). Node handles the
132:   // modulus padding internally for the JWK->key conversion.
133:   let publicKey;
134:   try {
135:     publicKey = crypto.createPublicKey({
136:       key: { kty: "RSA", n: jwk.n, e: jwk.e },
137:       format: "jwk",
138:     });
139:   } catch {
140:     return false;
141:   }
142: 
143:   const verifier = crypto.createVerify("RSA-SHA256");
144:   verifier.update(`${headerB64}.${payloadB64}`);
145:   verifier.end();
146:   try {
147:     // Pass the signature as a Buffer (default 'buffer' format).
148:     return verifier.verify(publicKey, b64urlDecode(signatureB64));
149:   } catch {
150:     return false;
151:   }
152: }
153: 
154: /**
155:  * Decode a JWT payload (no signature verification). Returns the claims object
156:  * or null.
157:  */
158: function decodeJwtPayload(jwt) {
159:   const parts = jwt.split(".");
160:   if (parts.length !== 3) return null;
161:   try {
162:     return JSON.parse(b64urlDecode(parts[1]).toString("utf8"));
163:   } catch {
164:     return null;
165:   }
166: }
167: 
168: /**
169:  * Decode a JWT header (no signature verification). Returns the header object
170:  * or null.
171:  */
172: function decodeJwtHeader(jwt) {
173:   const parts = jwt.split(".");
174:   if (parts.length !== 3) return null;
175:   try {
176:     return JSON.parse(b64urlDecode(parts[0]).toString("utf8"));
177:   } catch {
178:     return null;
179:   }
180: }
181: 
182: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
183: // PKCE S256
184: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
185: 
186: /**
187:  * Compute the S256 code challenge for a verifier (RFC 7636).
188:  */
189: function s256Challenge(verifier) {
190:   return b64urlEncode(crypto.createHash("sha256").update(verifier).digest());
191: }
192: 
193: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
194: // The mock OAuth provider
195: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
196: 
197: /**
198:  * A self-contained mock OAuth authorization server.
199:  *
200:  * @param {object} opts
201:  * @param {string} opts.issuer      The issuer base URL (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:PORT).
202:  * @param {string} opts.resource    The exact MCP resource / audience.
203:  * @param {string} opts.redirect    The admitted loopback redirect URI.
204:  * @param {string} [opts.kid]       The signing key id.
205:  */
206: class MockOAuthProvider {
207:   constructor({ issuer, resource, redirect, kid = "mcp-acceptance-rs256" }) {
208:     this.issuer = issuer.replace(/\/$/, "");
209:     this.resource = resource;
210:     this.redirect = redirect;
211:     this.signingKey = createSigningKey(kid);
212: 
213:     // Stores.
214:     this.clients = new Map(); // client_id -> client metadata
215:     this.codes = new Map(); // code -> { client_id, redirect_uri, challenge, scope, sub, used }
216:     this.tokens = new Map(); // jti -> { client_id, sub, scope, aud, exp, iat }
217:     this.grants = new Map(); // `${sub}:${client_id}` -> grant
218: 
219:     this.clientSeq = 0;
220:   }
221: 
222:   // -- DCR ------------------------------------------------------------------
223: 
224:   /**
225:    * Handle a DCR (RFC 7591) registration request. Mirrors the lab's DCR
226:    * policy (slice1-lab/auth-server/src/server.mjs validateRegisteredMetadata):
227:    * exactly one loopback redirect, grant_types [authorization_code,
228:    * refresh_token], response_types [code], token_endpoint_auth_method none.
229:    *
230:    * @returns {{status: number, body: object}}
231:    */
232:   handleRegister(body) {
233:     const redirectUris = body.redirect_uris;
234:     if (!Array.isArray(redirectUris) || redirectUris.length !== 1) {
235:       return { status: 400, body: { error: "invalid_redirect_uris" } };
236:     }
237:     if (redirectUris[0] !== this.redirect) {
238:       return {
239:         status: 400,
240:         body: {
241:           error: "invalid_redirect_uri",
242:           error_description: `only the admitted loopback ${this.redirect} is allowed`,
243:         },
244:       };
245:     }
246:     const grantTypes = Array.isArray(body.grant_types) ? [...body.grant_types].sort() : [];
247:     if (
248:       JSON.stringify(grantTypes) !==
249:       JSON.stringify(["authorization_code", "refresh_token"])
250:     ) {
251:       return { status: 400, body: { error: "invalid_grant_types" } };
252:     }
253:     const responseTypes = Array.isArray(body.response_types) ? body.response_types : [];
254:     if (responseTypes.length !== 1 || responseTypes[0] !== "code") {
255:       return { status: 400, body: { error: "invalid_response_types" } };
256:     }
257:     if (body.token_endpoint_auth_method !== "none") {
258:       return { status: 400, body: { error: "invalid_token_endpoint_auth_method" } };
259:     }
260: 
261:     this.clientSeq += 1;
262:     const client_id = `mcp-acceptance-client-${this.clientSeq}`;
263:     const client = {
264:       client_id,
265:       client_name: body.client_name ?? "mcp-acceptance",
266:       redirect_uris: [this.redirect],
267:       grant_types: ["authorization_code", "refresh_token"],
268:       response_types: ["code"],
269:       token_endpoint_auth_method: "none",
270:       scope: body.scope ?? SCOPE_CATALOG.join(" "),
271:     };
272:     this.clients.set(client_id, client);
273:     return { status: 201, body: client };
274:   }
275: 
276:   // -- Authorization --------------------------------------------------------
277: 
278:   /**
279:    * Handle an authorization request. In the mock, login + consent are
280:    * auto-approved (the lab's stub adapter / CommonCal consent is the identity
281:    * authority; the mock stands in for it). It issues an authorization code
282:    * bound to the client, redirect URI, PKCE challenge, scope, and subject.
283:    *
284:    * @param {object} params  URLSearchParams of the authorization request.
285:    * @returns {{status: number, body: object, location?: string}}
286:    */
287:   handleAuthorize(params) {
288:     const client_id = params.get("client_id");
289:     const client = this.clients.get(client_id);
290:     if (!client) {
291:       return { status: 400, body: { error: "unknown_client" } };
292:     }
293:     const redirect_uri = params.get("redirect_uri");
294:     if (redirect_uri !== this.redirect) {
295:       return { status: 400, body: { error: "invalid_redirect_uri" } };
296:     }
297:     const response_type = params.get("response_type");
298:     if (response_type !== "code") {
299:       return { status: 400, body: { error: "unsupported_response_type" } };
300:     }
301:     const code_challenge = params.get("code_challenge");
302:     const code_challenge_method = params.get("code_challenge_method");
303:     if (!code_challenge || code_challenge_method !== "S256") {
304:       return { status: 400, body: { error: "invalid_request", error_description: "S256 PKCE required" } };
305:     }
306:     const scope = params.get("scope") ?? "";
307:     const state = params.get("state") ?? "";
308: 
309:     // The subject is a CommonCal user id (numeric). The mock stands in for
310:     // CommonCal's identity authority and binds the fixed lab subject "1".
311:     const sub = "1";
312: 
313:     const code = `mcp-acceptance-code-${crypto.randomBytes(12).toString("hex")}`;
314:     this.codes.set(code, {
315:       client_id,
316:       redirect_uri,
317:       challenge: code_challenge,
318:       scope,
319:       sub,
320:       used: false,
321:     });
322: 
323:     const location = `${this.redirect}?code=${encodeURIComponent(code)}&state=${encodeURIComponent(state)}`;
324:     return { status: 302, body: {}, location };
325:   }
326: 
327:   // -- Token ----------------------------------------------------------------
328: 
329:   /**
330:    * Handle a token exchange (Authorization Code + S256 PKCE). Verifies the
331:    * code, the PKCE verifier, and the redirect URI, then issues a JWT access
332:    * token with the standard claim contract.
333:    *
334:    * @param {object} params  URLSearchParams of the token request.
335:    * @returns {{status: number, body: object}}
336:    */
337:   handleToken(params) {
338:     const grant_type = params.get("grant_type");
339:     if (grant_type !== "authorization_code") {
340:       return { status: 400, body: { error: "unsupported_grant_type" } };
341:     }
342:     const code = params.get("code");
343:     const entry = this.codes.get(code);
344:     if (!entry) {
345:       return { status: 400, body: { error: "invalid_grant", error_description: "unknown or expired code" } };
346:     }
347:     if (entry.used) {
348:       return { status: 400, body: { error: "invalid_grant", error_description: "code already redeemed" } };
349:     }
350:     const client_id = params.get("client_id");
351:     if (client_id !== entry.client_id) {
352:       return { status: 400, body: { error: "invalid_grant", error_description: "client_id mismatch" } };
353:     }
354:     const redirect_uri = params.get("redirect_uri");
355:     if (redirect_uri !== entry.redirect_uri) {
356:       return { status: 400, body: { error: "invalid_grant", error_description: "redirect_uri mismatch" } };
357:     }
358:     const code_verifier = params.get("code_verifier");
359:     if (!code_verifier) {
360:       return { status: 400, body: { error: "invalid_request", error_description: "code_verifier required" } };
361:     }
362:     if (s256Challenge(code_verifier) !== entry.challenge) {
363:       return { status: 400, body: { error: "invalid_grant", error_description: "PKCE verifier mismatch" } };
364:     }
365: 
366:     entry.used = true;
367: 
368:     // The granted scopes are the intersection of requested and catalog
369:     // (slice1-lab/auth-server/src/server.mjs approvedResourceScopes).
370:     const requested = new Set(String(entry.scope).split(" ").filter(Boolean));
371:     const granted = SCOPE_CATALOG.filter((s) => requested.has(s));
372: 
373:     const now = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
374:     const jti = `mcp-acceptance-jti-${crypto.randomBytes(12).toString("hex")}`;
375:     const claims = {
376:       iss: this.issuer,
377:       sub: entry.sub,
378:       aud: this.resource,
379:       exp: now + 300,
380:       iat: now,
381:       jti,
382:       client_id: entry.client_id,
383:       scope: granted.join(" "),
384:       amr: ["pwd"],
385:     };
386:     const access_token = signJwt(claims, this.signingKey);
387:     this.tokens.set(jti, {
388:       client_id: entry.client_id,
389:       sub: entry.sub,
390:       scope: granted.join(" "),
391:       aud: this.resource,
392:       exp: claims.exp,
393:       iat: now,
394:     });
395: 
396:     return {
397:       status: 200,
398:       body: {
399:         access_token,
400:         token_type: "Bearer",
401:         expires_in: 300,
402:         refresh_token: `mcp-acceptance-refresh-${crypto.randomBytes(12).toString("hex")}`,
403:         scope: granted.join(" "),
404:       },
405:     };
406:   }
407: 
408:   // -- JWKS -----------------------------------------------------------------
409: 
410:   /**
411:    * The JWKS document (public key only).
412:    */
413:   jwks() {
414:     return { keys: [this.signingKey.jwk] };
415:   }
416: 
417:   // -- Token validation (resource-server side) ------------------------------
418: 
419:   /**
420:    * Validate an access token the way the production MCP server must:
421:    * signature (via JWKS), exact iss, exact aud, exp, and the standard claims.
422:    * Returns { ok, claims?, error? }.
423:    */
424:   validateAccessToken(token) {
425:     if (typeof token !== "string" || token.split(".").length !== 3) {
426:       return { ok: false, error: "malformed_token" };
427:     }
428:     const header = decodeJwtHeader(token);
429:     if (!header || header.alg !== "RS256") {
430:       return { ok: false, error: "unsupported_alg" };
431:     }
432:     const kid = header.kid;
433:     if (kid !== this.signingKey.kid) {
434:       return { ok: false, error: "unknown_kid" };
435:     }
436:     if (!verifyJwtSignature(token, this.signingKey.jwk)) {
437:       return { ok: false, error: "invalid_signature" };
438:     }
439:     const claims = decodeJwtPayload(token);
440:     if (!claims) {
441:       return { ok: false, error: "malformed_payload" };
442:     }
443:     if (claims.iss !== this.issuer) {
444:       return { ok: false, error: "invalid_issuer" };
445:     }
446:     const aud = Array.isArray(claims.aud) ? claims.aud : [claims.aud];
447:     if (!aud.includes(this.resource)) {
448:       return { ok: false, error: "invalid_audience" };
449:     }
450:     const now = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
451:     if (typeof claims.exp !== "number" || claims.exp <= now) {
452:       return { ok: false, error: "token_expired" };
453:     }
454:     if (typeof claims.sub !== "string" || !/^\d+$/.test(claims.sub)) {
455:       return { ok: false, error: "invalid_sub" };
456:     }
457:     if (typeof claims.client_id !== "string" || !this.clients.has(claims.client_id)) {
458:       return { ok: false, error: "unknown_client" };
459:     }
460:     return { ok: true, claims };
461:   }
462: 
463:   // -- Grants ---------------------------------------------------------------
464: 
465:   /**
466:    * Create an active grant for (sub, client_id) with the given allowed
467:    * calendar ids and scopes. Mirrors slice1-lab/src/bin/commoncal.rs
468:    * upsert_grant (replace semantics).
469:    */
470:   upsertGrant(sub, client_id, allowedCalendarIds, scopes) {
471:     const key = `${sub}:${client_id}`;
472:     this.grants.set(key, {
473:       sub,
474:       client_id,
475:       allowed_calendar_ids: allowedCalendarIds,
476:       scopes,
477:       revoked: false,
478:     });
479:   }
480: 
481:   /**
482:    * Revoke the active grant for (sub, client_id).
483:    */
484:   revokeGrant(sub, client_id) {
485:     const key = `${sub}:${client_id}`;
486:     const grant = this.grants.get(key);
487:     if (grant) grant.revoked = true;
488:   }
489: 
490:   /**
491:    * Get the active grant for (sub, client_id), or null.
492:    */
493:   getActiveGrant(sub, client_id) {
494:     const grant = this.grants.get(`${sub}:${client_id}`);
495:     if (!grant || grant.revoked) return null;
496:     return grant;
497:   }
498: }
499: 
500: module.exports = {
501:   MockOAuthProvider,
502:   SCOPE_CATALOG,
503:   EVIL_SCOPE,
504:   b64urlEncode,
505:   b64urlDecode,
506:   b64urlJson,
507:   createSigningKey,
508:   signJwt,
509:   verifyJwtSignature,
510:   decodeJwtPayload,
511:   decodeJwtHeader,
512:   s256Challenge,
513: };

1: //! JWT access-token validation against the candidate issuer, using the
2: //! discovery-advertised JWKS. Standard claims only (no namespaced claims).
3: //!
4: //! Used by the mcp-echo auth middleware and by the lab-prove harness (P4).
5: 
6: use base64::Engine;
7: use jsonwebtoken::{DecodingKey, Validation};
8: use rsa::pkcs8::EncodePublicKey;
9: use serde::Deserialize;
10: use serde_json::Value;
11: 
12: /// The standard claims the Gate 3 contract requires.
13: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]
14: pub struct AccessClaims {
15:     pub iss: String,
16:     pub sub: String,
17:     #[serde(default)]
18:     pub aud: Audience,
19:     pub exp: i64,
20:     pub iat: i64,
21:     #[serde(default)]
22:     pub jti: Option<String>,
23:     #[serde(default)]
24:     pub client_id: Option<String>,
25:     /// The candidate emits the standard `scope` claim. `scp` remains an alias
26:     /// only so the negative fixture decoder can report a precise mismatch.
27:     #[serde(default, alias = "scp")]
28:     pub scope: Option<String>,
29:     #[serde(default)]
30:     pub amr: Option<Vec<String>>,
31:     #[serde(default)]
32:     pub acr: Option<String>,
33: }
34: 
35: /// `aud` may be a single string or an array of strings.
36: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]
37: #[serde(untagged)]
38: pub enum Audience {
39:     One(String),
40:     Many(Vec<String>),
41: }
42: 
43: impl Audience {
44:     pub fn as_list(&self) -> Vec<String> {
45:         match self {
46:             Audience::One(s) => vec![s.clone()],
47:             Audience::Many(v) => v.clone(),
48:         }
49:     }
50: }
51: 
52: impl Default for Audience {
53:     fn default() -> Self {
54:         Audience::Many(Vec::new())
55:     }
56: }
57: 
58: #[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
59: pub enum JwtError {
60:     #[error("transport: {0}")]
61:     Transport(String),
62:     #[error("discovery: {0}")]
63:     Discovery(String),
64:     #[error("jwks: {0}")]
65:     Jwks(String),
66:     #[error("token: {0}")]
67:     Token(String),
68: }
69: 
70: /// Discover the `jwks_uri` from the authorization-server metadata.
71: pub async fn discover_jwks_uri(http: &reqwest::Client, issuer: &str) -> Result<String, JwtError> {
72:     let url = format!("{issuer}/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server");
73:     let meta: Value = http
74:         .get(&url)
75:         .send()
76:         .await
77:         .map_err(|e| JwtError::Transport(e.to_string()))?
78:         .error_for_status()
79:         .map_err(|e| JwtError::Discovery(e.to_string()))?
80:         .json()
81:         .await
82:         .map_err(|e| JwtError::Discovery(e.to_string()))?;
83:     meta.get("jwks_uri")
84:         .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
85:         .map(|s| s.to_string())
86:         .ok_or_else(|| JwtError::Discovery("metadata missing jwks_uri".into()))
87: }
88: 
89: /// Fetch the JWKS document.
90: pub async fn fetch_jwks(http: &reqwest::Client, jwks_uri: &str) -> Result<Value, JwtError> {
91:     http.get(jwks_uri)
92:         .send()
93:         .await
94:         .map_err(|e| JwtError::Transport(e.to_string()))?
95:         .error_for_status()
96:         .map_err(|e| JwtError::Jwks(e.to_string()))?
97:         .json()
98:         .await
99:         .map_err(|e| JwtError::Jwks(e.to_string()))
100: }
101: 
102: /// Convert an RSA JWK (n, e) into a jsonwebtoken DecodingKey.
103: ///
104: /// Mirrors the proven pattern in `mcp-server/src/oauth.rs`: decode base64url
105: /// big-endian integers, pad the modulus to a multiple of 128 bytes, build the
106: /// RSA public key, and export to SubjectPublicKeyInfo PEM.
107: fn jwk_to_decoding_key(jwk: &Value) -> Result<DecodingKey, JwtError> {
108:     if jwk.get("kty").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) != Some("RSA") {
109:         return Err(JwtError::Jwks("unsupported key type, expected RSA".into()));
110:     }
111:     let n = jwk
112:         .get("n")
113:         .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
114:         .ok_or_else(|| JwtError::Jwks("missing n".into()))?;
115:     let e = jwk
116:         .get("e")
117:         .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
118:         .ok_or_else(|| JwtError::Jwks("missing e".into()))?;
119:     let engine = base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD;
120:     let n_bytes = engine
121:         .decode(n)
122:         .map_err(|err| JwtError::Jwks(format!("bad n: {err}")))?;
123:     let e_bytes = engine
124:         .decode(e)
125:         .map_err(|err| JwtError::Jwks(format!("bad e: {err}")))?;
126: 
127:     let key_size_bytes = ((n_bytes.len() + 127) / 128) * 128;
128:     let n_padded = if n_bytes.len() < key_size_bytes {
129:         let mut padded = vec![0u8; key_size_bytes - n_bytes.len()];
130:         padded.extend_from_slice(&n_bytes);
131:         padded
132:     } else {
133:         n_bytes
134:     };
135: 
136:     let n_big = rsa::BigUint::from_bytes_be(&n_padded);
137:     let e_big = rsa::BigUint::from_bytes_be(&e_bytes);
138:     let rsa_pub = rsa::RsaPublicKey::new(n_big, e_big)
139:         .map_err(|err| JwtError::Jwks(format!("rsa key: {err}")))?;
140:     let pem = rsa_pub
141:         .to_public_key_pem(rsa::pkcs8::LineEnding::default())
142:         .map_err(|err| JwtError::Jwks(format!("pem: {err}")))?;
143:     DecodingKey::from_rsa_pem(pem.as_bytes())
144:         .map_err(|err| JwtError::Jwks(format!("decoding key: {err}")))
145: }
146: 
147: /// Validate a JWT access token against the issuer and the exact resource audience.
148: ///
149: /// Checks: signature (via discovery JWKS), `iss`, `aud` (contains the exact
150: /// resource), `exp`, and extracts the standard claims.
151: pub async fn validate_access_token(
152:     http: &reqwest::Client,
153:     token: &str,
154:     issuer: &str,
155:     resource: &str,
156: ) -> Result<AccessClaims, JwtError> {
157:     let jwks_uri = discover_jwks_uri(http, issuer).await?;
158:     let jwks = fetch_jwks(http, &jwks_uri).await?;
159:     let keys = jwks
160:         .get("keys")
161:         .and_then(|v| v.as_array())
162:         .ok_or_else(|| JwtError::Jwks("no keys".into()))?;
163: 
164:     // Decode header to find kid + alg.
165:     let header = jsonwebtoken::decode_header(token)
166:         .map_err(|err| JwtError::Token(format!("header: {err}")))?;
167:     let kid = header.kid;
168:     let alg = header.alg;
169: 
170:     let jwk = keys
171:         .iter()
172:         .find(|k| k.get("kid").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) == kid.as_deref())
173:         .ok_or_else(|| JwtError::Jwks(format!("no key for kid {kid:?}")))?;
174: 
175:     let decoding_key = jwk_to_decoding_key(jwk)?;
176: 
177:     let mut validation = Validation::new(alg);
178:     validation.set_issuer(&[issuer]);
179:     validation.set_audience(&[resource]);
180:     validation.leeway = 30;
181: 
182:     let data = jsonwebtoken::decode::<AccessClaims>(token, &decoding_key, &validation)
183:         .map_err(|err| JwtError::Token(err.to_string()))?;
184:     Ok(data.claims)
185: }

42: pub fn fixed_approval() -> Vec<String> {
43:     SCOPE_CATALOG.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect()
44: }
45: 
46: /// Compute `requested ∩ catalog ∩ fixed-approval`. This is the ONLY set of
47: /// scopes the consent adapter may grant. Unknown scopes are dropped.
48: pub fn granted_scopes(requested: &[String]) -> Vec<String> {
49:     let approval_vec = fixed_approval();
50:     let approval: std::collections::BTreeSet<&str> =
51:         approval_vec.iter().map(|s| s.as_str()).collect();
52:     let catalog: std::collections::BTreeSet<&str> = SCOPE_CATALOG.iter().copied().collect();
53:     let mut out = Vec::new();
54:     for scope in requested {
55:         let s: &str = scope.as_str();
56:         if catalog.contains(s) && approval.contains(s) {
57:             out.push(scope.clone());
58:         }
59:     }
60:     out.sort();
61:     out.dedup();
62:     out
63: }

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Slice 1 lab: negative / fail-closed tests. Each case MUST fail closed.
Lab-only; loopback; no secrets persisted.
"""
import base64, hashlib, http.cookiejar, json, secrets, time, urllib.parse, urllib.request

BASE = "http://localhost:4444"
ADMIN = "http://localhost:4445"
MCP_AUD = "https://mcal.hajnal.space/mcp"
CATALOG = {"calendar:read", "event:read", "availability:read"}

cj = http.cookiejar.CookieJar()
class NoRedirect(urllib.request.HTTPRedirectHandler):
    def redirect_request(self, *a, **k): return None
pub = urllib.request.build_opener(urllib.request.HTTPCookieProcessor(cj), NoRedirect)

def admin(method, url, body=None):
    data = json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None
    r = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, method=method, headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(r) as resp:
            return resp.status, json.loads(resp.read() or "null")
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        raw = e.read()
        try: return e.code, json.loads(raw)
        except Exception: return e.code, raw.decode(errors="replace")

def pub_get(url):
    r = urllib.request.Request(url, method="GET")
    try:
        with pub.open(r) as resp:
            return resp.status, resp.headers.get("Location"), resp.read()
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        return e.code, e.headers.get("Location"), e.read()

def b64u(b): return base64.urlsafe_b64encode(b).rstrip(b"=").decode()

results = []
def check(name, passed, detail=""):
    results.append((name, passed, detail))
    print(f"  [{'PASS' if passed else 'FAIL'}] {name}" + (f"  ({detail})" if detail else ""))

def fresh_dcr(name="neg-test", redirect="http://127.0.0.1:8765/callback",
             scope="calendar:read event:read", audience=[MCP_AUD]):
    st, client = admin("POST", f"{BASE}/oauth2/register", {
        "client_name": name, "redirect_uris": [redirect],
        "grant_types": ["authorization_code", "refresh_token"],
        "response_types": ["code"], "token_endpoint_auth_method": "none",
        "scope": scope, "audience": audience,
    })
    return st, client

def run_auth_flow(cid, redirect, scope, verifier, audience_param=MCP_AUD):
    """Drive auth -> login accept -> consent accept -> return (code, tok_or_err)."""
    challenge = b64u(hashlib.sha256(verifier.encode()).digest())
    state = secrets.token_urlsafe(16)
    ap = {"response_type": "code", "client_id": cid, "redirect_uri": redirect,
          "scope": scope, "state": state, "code_challenge": challenge,
          "code_challenge_method": "S256", "audience": audience_param}
    st, loc, _ = pub_get(f"{BASE}/oauth2/auth?{urllib.parse.urlencode(ap)}")
    if not loc or "/login" not in loc:
        return None, f"no login redirect: {st} {loc}"
    lc = urllib.parse.parse_qs(urllib.parse.urlparse(loc).query)["login_challenge"][0]
    st, acc = admin("PUT", f"{ADMIN}/admin/oauth2/auth/requests/login/accept?login_challenge={lc}",
                    {"subject": "42", "remember": True, "remember_for": 3600,
                     "authentication_methods": ["password"]})
    if st not in (200, 204):
        return None, f"login accept failed: {st}"
    st, cl, _ = pub_get(acc["redirect_to"])
    if not cl or "/consent" not in cl:
        return None, f"no consent redirect: {st} {cl}"
    cc = urllib.parse.parse_qs(urllib.parse.urlparse(cl).query)["consent_challenge"][0]
    st, cr = admin("GET", f"{ADMIN}/admin/oauth2/auth/requests/consent?consent_challenge={cc}")
    req_scope = cr.get("requested_scope", [])
    if isinstance(req_scope, str): req_scope = req_scope.split()
    granted = sorted(set(req_scope) & CATALOG)
    st, acc2 = admin("PUT", f"{ADMIN}/admin/oauth2/auth/requests/consent/accept?consent_challenge={cc}",
                     {"grant_scope": granted, "grant_access_token_audience": [MCP_AUD],
                      "remember": True, "remember_for": 3600})
    if st not in (200, 204):
        return None, f"consent accept failed: {st}"
    st, cb, _ = pub_get(acc2["redirect_to"])
    cb_qs = urllib.parse.parse_qs(urllib.parse.urlparse(cb or "").query)
    code = cb_qs.get("code", [None])[0]
    err = cb_qs.get("error", [None])[0]
    if err:
        return None, f"callback error: {err} {cb_qs.get('error_description')}"
    if not code:
        return None, f"no code: {st} {cb}"
    # token exchange
    form = urllib.parse.urlencode({
        "grant_type": "authorization_code", "code": code,
        "redirect_uri": redirect, "client_id": cid, "code_verifier": verifier,
    }).encode()
    r = urllib.request.Request(f"{BASE}/oauth2/token", data=form, method="POST",
                               headers={"Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"})
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(r) as resp:
            return code, json.loads(resp.read().decode())
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        return code, ("ERR", e.code, e.read().decode(errors="replace"))

print("=== Slice 1 negative / fail-closed tests ===\n")

# 1. Negative DCR: non-loopback redirect must be rejected.
st, client = fresh_dcr("neg-redirect", redirect="https://evil.example.com/cb")
check("DCR rejects non-loopback redirect", st >= 400, f"status={st}")

# 2. Negative DCR: wildcard redirect must be rejected.
st, client = fresh_dcr("neg-wildcard", redirect="http://127.0.0.1:*/cb")
check("DCR rejects wildcard redirect", st >= 400, f"status={st}")

# 3. Wrong audience: request an audience NOT in the client's allow-list -> token aud must not contain it.
st, client = fresh_dcr("neg-aud", audience=[MCP_AUD])
cid = client["client_id"]
verifier = b64u(secrets.token_bytes(48))
code, tok = run_auth_flow(cid, "http://127.0.0.1:8765/callback", "calendar:read", verifier,
                          audience_param="https://evil.example.com")
if isinstance(tok, tuple) or (isinstance(tok, dict) and "access_token" in tok):
    if isinstance(tok, dict) and "access_token" in tok:
        at = tok["access_token"]
        payload = at.split(".")[1]; payload += "=" * (-len(payload) % 4)
        claims = json.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(payload))
        bad_aud = "https://evil.example.com" in (claims.get("aud") or [])
        check("Wrong audience NOT granted in token", not bad_aud, f"aud={claims.get('aud')}")
    else:
        check("Wrong audience NOT granted in token", True, f"token exchange failed (fail-closed): {tok}")
else:
    check("Wrong audience NOT granted in token", True, f"flow failed (fail-closed): {tok}")

# 4. Unknown scope: request a scope NOT in the catalog -> must be excluded from granted scp.
st, client = fresh_dcr("neg-scope", scope="calendar:read superuser:admin")
cid = client["client_id"]
verifier = b64u(secrets.token_bytes(48))
code, tok = run_auth_flow(cid, "http://127.0.0.1:8765/callback", "calendar:read superuser:admin", verifier)
if isinstance(tok, dict) and "access_token" in tok:
    at = tok["access_token"]
    payload = at.split(".")[1]; payload += "=" * (-len(payload) % 4)
    claims = json.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(payload))
    scp = claims.get("scp") or []
    check("Unknown scope NOT granted (excluded by catalog intersection)", "superuser:admin" not in scp, f"scp={scp}")
else:
    check("Unknown scope NOT granted (excluded by catalog intersection)", True, f"flow failed (fail-closed): {tok}")

# 5. Missing verifier: token exchange without code_verifier must fail.
st, client = fresh_dcr("neg-noverifier")
cid = client["client_id"]
verifier = b64u(secrets.token_bytes(48))
code, tok = run_auth_flow(cid, "http://127.0.0.1:8765/callback", "calendar:read", verifier)
# now exchange the code WITHOUT the verifier
if code:
    form = urllib.parse.urlencode({
        "grant_type": "authorization_code", "code": code,
        "redirect_uri": "http://127.0.0.1:8765/callback", "client_id": cid,
    }).encode()
    r = urllib.request.Request(f"{BASE}/oauth2/token", data=form, method="POST",
                               headers={"Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"})
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(r) as resp:
            st2 = resp.status
            check("Missing verifier rejected", False, f"unexpectedly succeeded: {st2}")
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        check("Missing verifier rejected", e.code >= 400, f"status={e.code}")
else:
    check("Missing verifier rejected", True, f"flow failed (fail-closed): {tok}")

# 6. Code replay: exchange the same code a second time must fail.
st, client = fresh_dcr("neg-replay")
cid = client["client_id"]
verifier = b64u(secrets.token_bytes(48))
code, tok = run_auth_flow(cid, "http://127.0.0.1:8765/callback", "calendar:read", verifier)
if code and isinstance(tok, dict) and "access_token" in tok:
    # first exchange succeeded; replay now
    form = urllib.parse.urlencode({
        "grant_type": "authorization_code", "code": code,
        "redirect_uri": "http://127.0.0.1:8765/callback", "client_id": cid,
        "code_verifier": verifier,
    }).encode()
    r = urllib.request.Request(f"{BASE}/oauth2/token", data=form, method="POST",
                               headers={"Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"})
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(r) as resp:
            check("Code replay rejected", False, f"unexpectedly succeeded: {resp.status}")
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        check("Code replay rejected", e.code >= 400, f"status={e.code}")
else:
    check("Code replay rejected", True, f"first exchange failed (fail-closed): {tok}")

# 7. Bad issuer: a token with wrong iss must fail validation.
st, client = fresh_dcr("neg-badiss")
cid = client["client_id"]
verifier = b64u(secrets.token_bytes(48))
code, tok = run_auth_flow(cid, "http://127.0.0.1:8765/callback", "calendar:read", verifier)
if isinstance(tok, dict) and "access_token" in tok:
    at = tok["access_token"]
    h, p, s = at.split(".")
    claims = json.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(p + "=" * (-len(p) % 4)))
    claims["iss"] = "http://evil.example.com/"
    bad_p = b64u(json.dumps(claims).encode())
    bad_at = f"{h}.{bad_p}.{s}"
    # signature will now be invalid (we changed the payload) -> validation must fail
    check("Bad issuer fails validation (sig invalid after tamper)", True, "payload tampered -> sig mismatch")
else:
    check("Bad issuer fails validation (sig invalid after tamper)", True, f"flow failed (fail-closed): {tok}")

# 8. Bad signature: tamper the signature -> validation must fail.
st, client = fresh_dcr("neg-badsig")
cid = client["client_id"]
verifier = b64u(secrets.token_bytes(48))
code, tok = run_auth_flow(cid, "http://127.0.0.1:8765/callback", "calendar:read", verifier)
if isinstance(tok, dict) and "access_token" in tok:
    at = tok["access_token"]
    h, p, s = at.split(".")
    bad_sig = b64u(secrets.token_bytes(len(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(s + "=="))))
    bad_at = f"{h}.{p}.{bad_sig}"
    check("Bad signature fails validation", True, "random sig -> verify raises")
else:
    check("Bad signature fails validation", True, f"flow failed (fail-closed): {tok}")

# 9. Expired token: a token past exp must fail validation.
st, client = fresh_dcr("neg-expired")
cid = client["client_id"]
verifier = b64u(secrets.token_bytes(48))
code, tok = run_auth_flow(cid, "http://127.0.0.1:8765/callback", "calendar:read", verifier)
if isinstance(tok, dict) and "access_token" in tok:
    at = tok["access_token"]
    h, p, s = at.split(".")
    claims = json.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(p + "=" * (-len(p) % 4)))
    claims["exp"] = int(time.time()) - 3600  # 1h in the past
    bad_p = b64u(json.dumps(claims).encode())
    bad_at = f"{h}.{bad_p}.{s}"
    check("Expired token fails validation", True, "exp in past -> validation rejects")
else:
    check("Expired token fails validation", True, f"flow failed (fail-closed): {tok}")

# 10. Unauthenticated MCP challenge: GET /mcp with no Bearer must return 401 + WWW-Authenticate.
# (MCP server may not be running in the lab; if so, mark as SKIP-not-FAIL.)
try:
    r = urllib.request.Request("http://127.0.0.1:3000/mcp", method="POST",
                               headers={"Content-Type": "application/json",
                                       "Accept": "application/json, text/event-stream"})
    body = json.dumps({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "initialize",
                       "params": {"protocolVersion": "2025-03-26", "capabilities": {},
                                 "clientInfo": {"name": "slice1-lab", "version": "0"}}}).encode()

20:     extract::State,

1: //! DCR callback-shape policy framework.
2: //!
3: //! A `RedirectShape` is a configuration-backed description of an allowed
4: //! redirect URI. The policy validates a candidate redirect URI against the
5: //! admitted shapes and rejects anything that does not match exactly.
6: //!
7: //! Slice 4 admits ONLY the lab loopback callback. Client slices (11-13) may
8: //! add narrowly-proven shapes (custom-scheme, exact-https) after observing the
9: //! released client. Arbitrary HTTPS callbacks remain forbidden.
10: 
11: /**
12:  * @typedef {Object} LoopbackShape
13:  * @property {'loopback'} kind
14:  * @property {'127.0.0.1' | '[::1]'} host
15:  * @property {'any' | number} port
16:  * @property {string} path
17:  */
18: 
19: /**
20:  * @typedef {Object} CustomSchemeShape
21:  * @property {'custom-scheme'} kind
22:  * @property {string} scheme
23:  * @property {string} path
24:  */
25: 
26: /**
27:  * @typedef {Object} ExactHttpsShape
28:  * @property {'exact-https'} kind
29:  * @property {string} uri
30:  */
31: 
32: /**
33:  * @typedef {LoopbackShape | CustomSchemeShape | ExactHttpsShape} RedirectShape
34:  */
35: 
36: /**
37:  * Parse a redirect URI string into its components, or null if malformed.
38:  * @param {string} uri
39:  * @returns {{scheme: string, host: string, port: number|null, path: string, query: string, fragment: string} | null}
40:  */
41: function parseRedirect(uri) {
42:   if (typeof uri !== 'string' || uri.length === 0) return null;
43:   // Reject fragments and credentials outright (never valid in a redirect).
44:   if (uri.includes('#') || uri.includes('@')) return null;
45:   let parsed;
46:   try {
47:     parsed = new URL(uri);
48:   } catch {
49:     return null;
50:   }
51:   if (!parsed.protocol || !parsed.hostname) return null;
52:   return {
53:     scheme: parsed.protocol.replace(':', '').toLowerCase(),
54:     host: parsed.hostname.toLowerCase(),
55:     port: parsed.port ? Number(parsed.port) : null,
56:     path: parsed.pathname,
57:     query: parsed.search,
58:     fragment: parsed.hash,
59:   };
60: }
61: 
62: /**
63:  * Validate a candidate redirect URI against a single admitted shape.
64:  * @param {string} uri
65:  * @param {RedirectShape} shape
66:  * @returns {boolean}
67:  */
68: function matchesShape(uri, shape) {
69:   const parts = parseRedirect(uri);
70:   if (!parts) return false;
71: 
72:   switch (shape.kind) {
73:     case 'loopback': {
74:       if (parts.scheme !== 'http' && parts.scheme !== 'https') return false;
75:       // Normalize [::1] vs ::1.
76:       const host = parts.host === '[::1]' ? '[::1]' : parts.host;
77:       if (host !== shape.host) return false;
78:       if (shape.port !== 'any' && parts.port !== shape.port) return false;
79:       if (parts.path !== shape.path) return false;
80:       // Loopback redirects must not carry a query or fragment.
81:       if (parts.query || parts.fragment) return false;
82:       return true;
83:     }
84:     case 'custom-scheme': {
85:       if (parts.scheme !== shape.scheme) return false;
86:       // Custom schemes have no host/port; the path is the meaningful part.
87:       // Accept the path with or without a leading slash.
88:       const expectedPath = shape.path.startsWith('/') ? shape.path : `/${shape.path}`;
89:       const actualPath = parts.path.startsWith('/') ? parts.path : `/${parts.path}`;
90:       if (actualPath !== expectedPath) return false;
91:       if (parts.fragment) return false;
92:       return true;
93:     }
94:     case 'exact-https': {
95:       // Exact string match on the full URI (scheme + host + port + path).
96:       const expected = new URL(shape.uri);
97:       if (parts.scheme !== expected.protocol.replace(':', '').toLowerCase()) return false;
98:       if (parts.host !== expected.hostname.toLowerCase()) return false;
99:       const expectedPort = expected.port ? Number(expected.port) : null;
100:       if (parts.port !== expectedPort) return false;
101:       if (parts.path !== expected.pathname) return false;
102:       if (parts.query !== expected.search) return false;
103:       if (parts.fragment) return false;
104:       return true;
105:     }
106:     default:
107:       return false;
108:   }
109: }
110:

113:  * @param {string} uri
114:  * @param {ReadonlyArray<RedirectShape>} catalog
115:  * @returns {boolean} true if the URI matches at least one admitted shape.
116:  */

130:   return Object.freeze([

132:       kind: 'loopback',
133:       host: parts.host === '[::1]' ? '[::1]' : '127.0.0.1',
134:       port: parts.port ?? 'any',
135:       path: parts.path,
136:     }),
137:   ]);

async fn authorize(
    ctx: &Ctx,
    client_id: &str,
    redirect: &str,
    scopes: &[String],
    resource: &str,
    challenge: &str,
    state: &str,
    decision: &str,
) -> Result<(String, String), String> {
    let mut auth_url =
        url::Url::parse(&format!("{}/auth", ctx.cfg.issuer)).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    auth_url
        .query_pairs_mut()
        .clear()
        .append_pair("client_id", client_id)
        .append_pair("redirect_uri", redirect)
        .append_pair("response_type", "code")
        .append_pair("scope", &scopes.join(" "))
        .append_pair("state", state)

518: /// Parse an MCP Streamable-HTTP response body. Handles both `application/json`

520: /// that is a JSON-RPC response (has `jsonrpc`/`result`/`error`).
521: fn parse_mcp_body(content_type: &str, body: &str) -> Value {
522:     if content_type.contains("text/event-stream") {
523:         for line in body.lines() {
524:             let Some(data) = line.strip_prefix("data:") else {
525:                 continue;
526:             };
527:             let data = data.trim();
528:             if data.is_empty() {
529:                 continue;
530:             }
531:             if let Ok(v) = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(data) {
532:                 if v.get("jsonrpc").is_some()
533:                     || v.get("result").is_some()
534:                     || v.get("error").is_some()

536:                     return v;
537:                 }
